8:15 when I went to Cuba a while ago as a child, I went to go visit a beach with my uncles and we ended up swimming around a small Bay area. Coincidentally there was a hotel not too far from this beach and they claimed it as their own. We couldn't even see the hotel from where we were sitting. They told us to leave or they would call the police. As a kid I didn't really understand, I was only 13. But immediately my uncle's new and they got afraid and they took me back to my grandma's. 

The normal people there can't actually have any fun. At most what they can do is drink a lot and maybe share in some of the tech that they might have lying around. On my street everyone in their houses would come out to the middle of town, where someone had a projector out playing music videos. Everyone would be listening to the music watching the show and drinking and just dancing and having a good time. It was definitely drinking to forget how bad things really were. 

Granted this is just an emotional anecdotal story. And things have begun to escalate in Cuba here recently, at least according to my family who live there still. But you can still see the statistics.
